title: Next.js Ships Out-of-Band Patch for Two Critical RCE Flaws in Caching and SVG Processing
summary: Next.js released a security update fixing two critical flaws that could allow attackers to run harmful code remotely. This matters because it threatens applications built with the framework.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you develop websites or manage a service using Next.js, your engineering team needs to update the software immediately.
action_it: Apply the out-of-band security updates released by Next.js to address the critical remote code execution and denial-of-service flaws.

title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules
summary: Drupal fixed a critical security flaw in its software that could allow hackers to take over website servers when combined with certain add-on modules. Website administrators need to update their Drupal installations immediately.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you run a website powered by Drupal, you will need to ask your web administrator or IT team to update the software.
action_it: Apply the security patches released on October 14 by updating to Drupal versions 11.4.10, 11.3.19, or 10.6.19 depending on your branch, and review your site for any suspicious activity involving contributed modules and the Field UI component.

title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a security flaw in its PAN-OS software that is actively being used in attacks. This vulnerability allows attackers to run malicious code remotely on vulnerable firewalls.

also_covered.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Palo Alto Networks equipment, your IT and security teams will need to handle this update.
action_it: Apply the security updates released by Palo Alto Networks for PAN-OS to address CVE-2026-0322.

title: Fake Arch Linux packages push malware with root privileges
summary: Malicious software disguised as popular tools was uploaded to the Arch User Repository, a community platform for Arch Linux. This matters because installing these fake packages could give hackers full control over your computer.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you use Arch Linux and recently installed the 'yay' or 'paru' helper tools from the AUR, check your system for unauthorized changes and remove the malicious packages immediately.
action_it: Review Arch User Repository (AUR) packages for unauthorized or suspicious installations of 'yay' and 'paru', check affected systems for signs of compromise, and ensure administrative privileges have not been granted to unknown third parties.

title: Citizen Lab Traces Zero-Click Candiru Spyware Infections at Al Jazeera to Targeted Online Ads
summary: Researchers discovered that spyware made by the Israeli company Candiru infected devices at Al Jazeera using hidden online ads that required no user interaction. This matters because it shows how advanced spyware can silently compromise targets simply by loading a webpage.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything, as these targeted attacks are typically aimed at specific journalists and high-risk individuals. Using an up-to-date web browser and an ad blocker can help reduce overall exposure to malicious online advertisements.
action_it: Monitor network traffic and endpoint telemetry for anomalous connections related to known spyware infrastructure. Ensure all browsers and operating systems across the organization are kept strictly up to date, and consider deploying robust ad-blocking or content-filtering solutions on high-risk employee devices.

title: NGINX Fixes 5 Flaws, Including Possible RCE and a TLS Bug That May Skip Client-Cert Checks
summary: NGINX released updates to fix five security flaws, including memory bugs that could potentially allow attackers to run unauthorized code. These issues require specific configurations to be exploited.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses NGINX to run websites or services, your IT team should handle the update.
action_it: Upgrade NGINX to version 1.30.6 or 1.31.7 to apply the fixes for the five identified vulnerabilities.

title: Fake AI Attacks Spread Across US Companies: How MSSPs Can Stop Incidents Early
summary: Attackers are tricking people with fake artificial intelligence products to spread malicious software and steal account access. This trend is putting extra pressure on the companies that monitor security for American businesses.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. Be very careful when downloading new AI software or tools, making sure you are getting them from official and trusted sources.
action_it: Monitor endpoints and network traffic for suspicious software disguised as popular AI tools. Review browser session security and access controls.

title: Hackers hijack D-Link, Ubiquiti devices to resell your stolen bandwidth
summary: Hackers are taking control of internet routers and network devices in 34 countries to secretly sell access to victims' internet connections. This slows down your internet and can make your connection appear to be involved in illegal online activity.

title: Silent Lynx Exploits WinRAR Flaw to Deploy Reverse Shell in CIS Government Attacks
summary: A hacking group called Silent Lynx has been attacking government organizations in the CIS region using malicious files and software tools. This matters because it shows ongoing targeted attacks against government networks using common utilities to hide malicious activity.

title: Help TDS Linked to Hotejka as 20,000+ Cloudflare Pages Domains Host Tech Support Scams
summary: Over 20,000 Cloudflare Pages domains are hosting technical support scams using a long-running routing system called Help TDS. This operation directs unsuspecting users to fraudulent websites via compromised sites and cloud infrastructure.

title: ThreatsDay: Adobe RCE, DNS Wallet Theft, NVIDIA Container Escape, Self-Healing Backdoor + 23 More
summary: A weekly security roundup highlights various new threats, including a data theft tool with a built-in scaring feature and other recent vulnerabilities. These stories show how everyday permissions and trusted logins can be abused by attackers.

title: Is AI pentesting as good as a human pentester?
summary: An analysis compares artificial intelligence penetration testing with human testers, highlighting strengths and weaknesses of both approaches. The report helps organizations understand where AI security tools can be effective and where they fall short.

title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2022 reached end of mainstream support
summary: Microsoft's Windows Server 2022 has reached the end of mainstream support. The system will continue to receive security updates under extended support until October 2031.

title: Police arrests 95 suspects in international CSAM crackdown action
summary: Police across 17 countries arrested 95 suspects in an international operation targeting online groups that share child sexual abuse material. This law enforcement crackdown disrupts networks distributing illegal content.

title: Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation
summary: Artificial intelligence tools used in digital investigations are becoming overly confident in their own results faster than humans can verify them. This creates a risk of unverified errors spreading beyond a single workstation.
